title: Finite bounded-degree Q3 Friedrichs form closure and volume-uniform shifted order
question: For a fixed finite Q3 graph with bounded degree, do the exact onsite and bond forms have a common Friedrichs form domain and a volume-uniform shifted form order?

model.core: D=C_c^infinity(R^S) for a finite graph S, with q_i multiplication and p_i=-i*d/dq_i
model.closure_argument: The real polynomial potential is locally integrable and bounded below; the negative part is bounded, so the standard semibounded Schrodinger form theorem closes the C_c^infinity form and gives its Friedrichs operator.
model.common_domain_argument: Bond positivity gives Q_edge subset Q_on; the EXP-001129 envelope and the per-site shift 17/12 give B <= (10/3) sum_edges(K_i+K_j), hence Q_on subset Q_edge for graphs of degree at most six.
model.shifted_order: K_on=H_on+(17/12)|S| I and K_edge=K_on+B satisfy K_on <= K_edge <= 21 K_on for max degree six.

adversarial_review.check: chi and g are positive, c and lambda are nonnegative, the polynomial potential is real and locally integrable, and its negative part is bounded by the exact onsite square completion.
Bond positivity gives only Q_edge subset Q_on; the reverse inclusion is supplied separately by the quartic envelope after the per-site shift.
The 21 multiplier uses only the degree bound six and the per-site shift, not the number of vertices; it is a form bound, not a dynamics or gap bound.
Friedrichs operators are obtained for each fixed finite graph from the closed form theorem; arbitrary weighted products with unbounded observables are not asserted to have a common operator domain.
R302 reuses the compiled R300 polynomial envelope and checks the new rational shift/order constants; it does not formalize the representation theorem or thermodynamic limits.
Cutoff/beta modular transfer, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.

qft_interface.open: Weighted product-domain identities, cutoff/beta modular transfer, exact CCR domain transfer, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, exhaustion-independent common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS identification, a sector gap, continuum and the Pre-A production gate.
